string.text: Turns every castle into a small trading settlement. The castle stays a castle: same walls and the same noble recruits from its villages. Rebellion is a separate switch.
Adds a tavern room to the castle and a menu option to visit it. Tavern staff use the town tavern scenes.
On by default, even with Enable castle markets off. Removes any brothel location, such as Captivity Events', from castles. Turn this off to let another mod keep a brothel in castles.
On by default. A castle uses the same loyalty rebellion check as a town. Turn this off and castles go back to never rebelling.
On by default. Master switch for quests from castle merchants and artisans, and for village quests that point to a castle. Pick single quests in the Castle quests group.
On by default. Daily defaults only. Slacken Garrison becomes Festival and Games (+3 loyalty a day), and Irrigation gives 1 village hearth a day instead of 0.5. Off restores vanilla.
On by default. Construction projects only. Castellan's Office also adds 3%, 6% and 12% tax, and castles gain a Marketplace with 4%, 8% and 12% tariffs and better caravan access. Off restores vanilla.
Only matters with Hot Butter installed. On by default. Castle taverns get Hot Butter's tavern options, with the same rules as in towns.

Only matters with Improved Garrisons installed. On by default. Its button moves into Go to the castle, its tooltips show castle tariffs and tax, and its parties recruit and trade at castles as in towns. Its files are never changed.

On by default. Unhired companions also appear in castle taverns: a small group once, then companions move between towns and nearby castles over time. Works with the base game and most companion mods. Turn this off to send them back to towns, or if a companion mod misbehaves in castles. Needs Add a tavern.
Daily chance that an unhired companion in a town moves to a nearby castle that has none. Default 100. Arrivals stop once castles hold a third of the free companions. 0 stops arrivals.
Daily chance that a companion in a castle goes back to a nearby town. Default 10. 0 keeps them in castles until they are hired.
Days before a companion moved by this mod can move again. Default 7. Ignored when a castle stops hosting companions.
On by default. Caravans, including yours, can trade at castles the mod covers as they do in towns, and visits count toward trade agreements. Off: caravans trade only in towns.

On by default. Covers castles of other clans in your kingdom, and lets their lords recruit at castles. Your own clan's castles are always covered. Off returns those castles to vanilla: what the mod added is removed and workshops you own there are sold.
Apply to other kingdoms and clans

On by default. Covers castles of clans outside your kingdom, or every castle you do not own if you have no kingdom, and lets their lords and caravans recruit at castles. Off returns those castles to vanilla: what the mod added is removed and workshops you own there are sold.
Merchants per castle. Default 2, as in a town. Merchants can form caravans and give recruits. Lowering it moves extra merchants the mod created to a town.
Artisans per castle. Default 2; a town has 1. Artisans own workshops and give recruits. Lowering it moves extra artisans the mod created to a town.
Workshops per castle, from 0 to 8. Default 2. Lowering it removes only slots the mod added, never one owned by you or a lord.

Workshops per town, from 4 to 10. Default 4, as in the base game, where one is the artisans' own and cannot be bought. Slots above 4 work like any workshop but have no building in the town scene. The base game's 4 are never removed.
Extra town workshops you may own on top of the base game's limit of clan tier + 1. Default 0. Lowering it never takes a workshop away.

Extra castle workshops you may own on top of the castle limit of clan tier + 1. Default 0. The castle limit is separate from towns, so mods that change the town limit do not change it. Lowering it never takes a workshop away.
Off by default. On uses Castle workshop limit below instead of clan tier + 1 and Extra castle workshop limit, whatever your clan tier.
How many castle workshops you may own while Fixed castle workshop limit is on. Default 10. Lowering it never takes a workshop away.
Off by default. Removes the castle workshop limit, whatever the settings above say.
Gold given to a merchant this mod creates, if they have less. Vanilla caravans need a large purse before a notable will form one.
Applied once per castle: lower prosperity is raised to this. Default 1000, the top of the vanilla castle range; towns are about 1700 to 5600. 0 leaves prosperity alone.
Applied once per castle. The market starts with this share of the nearest town's trade goods. Default 25. Later stock comes from production, caravans and trade.
Each day the castle market gains this share of its villages' production, scaled by prosperity. The villages still send their full output to their town. Default 20. 0 turns it off.
How much a castle's people use up each day, compared with a town of the same prosperity. Default 50.
Safety cap. Castle production stops once the castle holds this share of its town's stock of a good. Default 60. Goods brought by caravans are not capped.
Sell castle surplus to its town
On by default. Like villagers, the castle sells goods its villages make beyond its reserve to their town and keeps the gold.
How many days of its own production or consumption, whichever is larger, the castle keeps of each good it produces before selling the rest to its town. Default 10.
On by default. Caravans rate castles low on goods higher as trade stops, so empty castles fill up. Needs Caravans trade at castles.
Largest boost to a caravan's rating of a nearly empty castle. Default 25. It shrinks to 0 as the castle reaches 35 percent of its town's trade goods.
Siege food from the castle market
On by default. A besieged castle that runs out of food uses its market's food, as a town does.
On by default. Lords can buy castle food above the castle's siege reserve, and travel to castles with food to spare. Off: they buy food only in towns and villages.
Castle prosperity tax, compared with a town of the same prosperity. Default 80. Town tax policies and perks also apply to castles.
In towns, goods sold in the market raise prosperity. Castles get this share of that effect. Default 50. Prosperity in turn raises tax. 0 keeps it town-only, as in vanilla.
On by default. Needs the castle tavern. Town healing perks work while resting in a castle, and the governor's Medicine speeds garrison healing, as in a town.
On by default. Like towns and villages, a castle slowly restores its settlement health after raids or sieges, with Clean Infrastructure and In Best Light working as in a town.
On by default. Adds Enter smithy to the castle menu, as in towns but without smithing orders. Off hides it.

On by default. Adds Recruit troops to the castle menu. Castle merchants and artisans offer volunteers, and lords recruit there too; the Apply to switches decide which clans may. Off stops castle volunteers.
Chance that a new castle volunteer starts on the noble troop line. Default 50; towns are 0 and castle villages 100.
How fast the castle's merchants and artisans produce volunteers, compared with a town notable. Village recruits are unchanged, including the noble troops from castle villages.
Construction cost of the castle Marketplace, compared with a town Marketplace. Default 60. Only changes construction that has not been done yet.
Merchant quest. On by default. Needs low security at the castle, as in a town. Quests already running are not affected.
Merchant quest. On by default. Needs a bandit hideout near the castle, as in a town. Quests already running are not affected.
Artisan quest. On by default. Needs a raw material to be expensive in the castle market, as in a town. Quests already running are not affected.

Artisan quest from the base game. On by default. Needs a merchant in the same castle and a nearby town or covered castle to deliver to. If the destination is a covered castle whose market gate is blocked while the quest is active (refused entry, disguise, or face charges), you can pay the guards to take the goods in for half the reward. Quests already running are not affected.

Merchant or artisan quest from the base game. On by default. The notable must own at least one caravan, as in a town. Castles have no port, so it is always the land version. Quests already running are not affected.

Merchant quest from the base game. On by default. Needs a castle village, low castle security, a nearby hideout and a merchant with low mercy or honor, as in a town. Quests already running are not affected.

Village quest from the base game. On by default. A headman or landowner of a village owned by a castle can ask you to win back a land deed lost at a board game in the castle tavern. Needs the castle tavern. Quests already running are not affected.

Village quest from the base game. On by default. A headman of a horse, cattle or sheep village owned by a castle can offer it, and castle merchants and artisans can be the buyer you deliver the herd to. If that castle's market gate is blocked while the quest is active (refused entry, disguise, or face charges), you can pay the guards to take the herd in for half the reward. Quests already running are not affected.

Village quest from the base game. On by default. A landowner of a village owned by a castle can ask for help with a feud against another village of the same castle. Quests already running are not affected.

On by default. Adds Visit the castle trainers to Go to the castle. You and the companions and adult family members in your party can pay to raise skills or an attribute, with a cooldown. Gains are permanent and stay if the mod is removed.
On by default. You can train at the castle.
On by default. Adult companions and family members of your clan who are in your party can train. Heroes elsewhere, prisoners and visiting lords cannot.
Gold for one skill training session, however many heroes train in it. Default 1000.
Your clan's influence for one skill training session. Default 10.
Most random skills of the chosen group each hero improves in one session. Default 3. Only skills below the maximum trainable level are picked, so a hero with fewer of them improves fewer.
Fewest levels a trained skill gains. Default 2. If it is above the maximum, the two are swapped.

Most levels a trained skill gains. Default 10. Levels are added directly: learning limits and focus points do not reduce them, and they give no character experience, so heroes do not level up from training.
Training never raises a skill above this level; beyond it, heroes must learn by doing. Default 150.
Days a hero waits after a skill training session before the next one, at any castle. Default 7.

On by default. Adds Train an attribute to the castle trainers: pick one hero and one attribute to raise by 1, never above the game's maximum. It has its own cost and cooldown, separate from skill training.
Gold for raising one attribute by 1. Default 5000.
Your clan's influence for raising one attribute by 1. Default 25.
Days a hero waits after raising an attribute before raising another, at any castle. Default 7.
You are in the castle tavern. Off-duty soldiers, traders and travellers share the benches.
Disguise yourself and sneak through the castle gate. ({SNEAK_CHANCE}%)
The guards offer to take the herd in for you and hand it to the buyer inside, but they will keep a cut of the payment. You would receive {GUARD_HERD_REWARD}{GOLD_ICON}.
You do not have the full herd with you.
The guards offer to take the {PRODUCT} in for you and hand it to the buyer inside, but they will keep a cut of the payment. You would receive {GUARD_ARTISAN_REWARD}{GOLD_ICON}.
You do not have all of the {PRODUCT} with you.
{SETTLEMENT} no longer has a castle market, so this task there was called off.
The castle's drillmaster and the steward's clerks will teach you, your companions and your adult family members, for a price.
No one in your party can train here. Check Train yourself and Train companions in the mod options.
No one trains while the castle is under siege.
No one is ready to train yet. The next hero is ready {WHEN}.
Everyone ready to train already has these skills at {LEVEL} or higher.
{HEROES} will each gain {LOW} to {HIGH} levels in up to {COUNT} random {?(COUNT > 1)}skills{?}skill{\?} from: {SKILLS}. Only skills below {LEVEL} are trained, and none goes above it.
This costs {GOLD}{GOLD_ICON} and {INFLUENCE} influence. Each trained hero then waits {DAYS} days before training skills again.
Everyone ready to train already has every attribute at the maximum of {LEVEL}.
Pick one hero and one attribute to raise by 1, up to the maximum of {LEVEL}.
Every attribute is at the maximum of {LEVEL}.
Raise {HERO}'s {ATTRIBUTE} from {OLD} to {NEW} for {GOLD}{GOLD_ICON} and {INFLUENCE} influence? {HERO} then waits {DAYS} days before training an attribute again.
You have reached the maximum number of town workshops you can have.
You have reached the maximum number of castle workshops you can have.
{SETTLEMENT} no longer has a castle market, so your {COUNT} {?(COUNT > 1)}workshops there were{?}workshop there was{\?} sold for {GOLD}{GOLD_ICON}.
Hot Butter could not run in the castle tavern.
The castle tavern could not be opened.
